topics.title: What business development is
topics.technical: Business development creates long-term value through customers, markets and relationships — the overlap of sales, marketing, strategy and partnerships. It is finding and building the ways a company grows, not just closing this week's deal.
topics.simple: Finding and building the paths a company grows along — partners, markets, deals.

topics.title: Understanding your market
topics.technical: Market research sizes the opportunity (TAM/SAM/SOM), maps segments and studies competitors. Building for a market you have not understood is the commonest and most expensive mistake.
topics.simple: Learning who might buy, how many there are, and who else is selling to them.

topics.title: The customer and their problem
topics.technical: Value starts from a real customer pain, discovered through interviews and observation, not assumed. Selling a solution to a problem nobody has is the graveyard of good products.
topics.simple: Finding the genuine pain people will pay to remove — by asking, not guessing.

topics.title: Value proposition
topics.technical: A value proposition states who you help, what problem you solve, and why you over alternatives. Sharp positioning makes selling easy; fuzzy positioning makes even good products hard to move.
topics.simple: One clear sentence: who you help, how, and why you beat the alternatives.

topics.title: Lead generation
topics.technical: Filling the pipeline uses inbound (content, SEO, referrals) and outbound (targeted outreach) channels. Quantity without qualification wastes effort; the goal is the right prospects, not the most.
topics.simple: Getting a steady stream of the right potential customers to talk to.

topics.title: Qualifying prospects
topics.technical: Frameworks like BANT (budget, authority, need, timeline) separate real opportunities from time-sinks. Disciplined qualification is what keeps a pipeline honest and a calendar productive.
topics.simple: Spotting early which prospects are real so you don't chase dead ends.

topics.title: The sales process
topics.technical: Deals move through stages — prospect, discover, present, handle objections, close, follow up — and tracking that flow reveals where they stall. A named process turns lucky wins into repeatable ones.
topics.simple: The repeatable steps from first contact to signed deal.

topics.title: Communication and discovery calls
topics.technical: Discovery is listening: open questions, active listening and understanding needs before pitching. The best salespeople talk least and diagnose most.
topics.simple: Winning by understanding the customer first, then talking.

topics.title: Negotiation
topics.technical: Negotiation seeks value for both sides: knowing your BATNA, anchoring thoughtfully, and trading concessions rather than caving. Win-lose deals cost the relationship that business development exists to build.
topics.simple: Reaching a deal both sides are glad to sign — without giving everything away.

topics.title: Building relationships
topics.technical: Trust compounds: consistent follow-through, genuine help and long horizons turn contacts into partners and referrers. Relationship capital is the asset that outlasts any single deal.
topics.simple: Turning contacts into lasting partnerships by being reliably useful.

topics.title: Partnerships and alliances
topics.technical: Strategic partnerships extend reach through others' customers and capabilities; clear mutual value and defined terms keep them alive. A good partnership multiplies effort; a vague one drains it.
topics.simple: Growing by teaming up with others who reach customers you cannot.

topics.title: Pricing strategy
topics.technical: Price signals value and shapes demand: cost-plus, value-based and competitive models each fit different situations, and underpricing can hurt as much as overpricing. Price is a positioning decision.
topics.simple: Setting a price that reflects value and shapes who buys.

topics.title: Marketing fundamentals
topics.technical: The 4Ps — product, price, place, promotion — and the funnel from awareness to purchase frame how demand is created. Business development and marketing feed each other or starve together.
topics.simple: How companies create and capture demand — the levers behind every sale.

topics.title: Digital channels
topics.technical: Content, social, email and SEO reach modern buyers where they research; each channel has its own economics and metrics. Choosing a few channels well beats spreading thin across all.
topics.simple: Reaching buyers online where they already look — through content, search and email.

topics.title: Metrics and analytics
topics.technical: CAC, LTV, conversion and pipeline velocity turn activity into a scoreboard; decisions guided by numbers beat decisions guided by opinions. What you do not measure, you cannot improve.
topics.simple: The numbers that show whether growth efforts are actually working.

topics.title: CRM and pipeline management
topics.technical: A CRM records every contact, deal and next step so nothing falls through cracks; a clean pipeline forecasts revenue honestly. The tool is only as good as the discipline behind it.
topics.simple: One system that tracks every deal and reminds you what's next.

topics.title: Proposals and closing
topics.technical: Proposals restate value, scope and price clearly; closing asks for the decision directly and handles the final objection. Deals die in ambiguity — clarity and a clear ask move them.
topics.simple: Putting the offer in writing and confidently asking for the yes.

topics.title: Account management and retention
topics.technical: Keeping customers costs less than winning them: onboarding, ongoing value and upselling grow accounts over time. Churn quietly undoes all acquisition; retention is where profit lives.
topics.simple: Keeping and growing customers you already won — cheaper than finding new ones.

topics.title: Business models
topics.technical: Subscription, marketplace, freemium and transactional models shape unit economics and growth. Understanding the model reveals which metrics matter and where the business actually makes money.
topics.simple: How a business actually makes money — and why the model changes everything.

topics.title: Strategy and planning
topics.technical: Strategy chooses where to play and how to win with limited resources; goals, priorities and honest review turn ambition into direction. A plan nobody revisits is decoration.
topics.simple: Deciding where to focus, and reviewing honestly whether it worked.

topics.title: The capstone
topics.technical: Build a go-to-market plan for a real product: market and customer analysis, value proposition, pricing, channels, metrics and a 90-day action plan. A concrete plan is what demonstrates the skill.
topics.simple: One realistic plan to take a product to market — the proof you can do the job.
